title: Figure 2.2: Total compute used during training
extracted_text:
Based on the analysis in Scaling Laws For [KMH+20] we train much larger models on many fewer tokens than is typical. As a consequence, our model is almost 10x larger than RoBERTa-Large (355M params), both models took roughly 50 percent of the compute during pre-training. Methodology for these calculations can be found in Appendix D.

Table 2.2: Datasets used to train GPT-3. "Weight in training mix" refers to the fraction of our training batches that are drawn from a given dataset, which we intentionally do not make proportional to the size. As a result, when we train for 300 billion tokens, some datasets are seen up to 3.4 times during training, while others are seen less than once.
